subject: 🏃 Sunday — 10 mi Long Run (Wk 3)
html:
Tomorrow: 10 mi long run on the Bayfront, 8:45–9:15 pace, HR 140–155 (Z2–low Z3). Pure aerobic time-on-feet — flat route, no MP segments, no progression finish. This is the longest run since Bay to Breakers (9.33 mi) and the first at this distance on purpose rather than by accident.

Pre-run activation (5 min): Quadruped hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, plus the PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side). If you haven't done the missed PT block from Friday yet (side plank w/ hip abduction, dead bug w/ banded pulldown, chin tuck + lifts), do it before you head out — five minutes, non-negotiable.

Execution: HR is the anchor. On the flat Bayfront the temptation is to let pace drift under 8:45 — resist it. If HR is sitting at 142 and pace is 8:50, you're nailing it. If pace creeps to 8:20 with HR at 150, you're working too hard for a long-run day. Polar H10 on — we need a clean 90-min HR trace.

Focus cue: Cadence over stride length. Keep turnover quick and light (aim 165+ SPM) rather than reaching with a longer stride — that's what protects the knee at mile 8 when fatigue sets in.

Superblast 3 test: Second run in the new shoes, first at real distance. Pay attention to how they feel at miles 7–8 when your foot is fatigued — any hot spots, any loss of that springy feel, any arch compression. Good data for the shoe rotation going forward.

Context: Week 3 of 12, Phase 1 Foundation — 63 days to race day. Six straight sessions at knee 1/5 since B2B recovery. W4 next week brings the PAL 10K taper with the benchmark race on Saturday May 30. Today's long run is the last real volume session before that taper starts. No gut training protocol yet (starts Week 5) — just eat a normal pre-run breakfast and bring water.

Tonight: Carb-forward dinner, good hydration, bed by 10. Lay out the H10 strap with your kit so you don't forget it at 6 AM.
